messages:
alex_support: Heads-up — Beth from Acme reported failures hitting the embeddings endpoint in bulk. Error seen: \"Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1538\" on ~10% of batched requests. Customer says it started after they upgraded SDKs overnight. Repro steps and logs below.

beth_acme: We're running a nightly job that sends ~12k texts in batches of 128 via our Python worker pool. It used to be stable. After upgrading to our latest image (which bumps the python SDK to 1.2.2 and ts-sdk to 0.9.8) we started getting these mismatches and a few timeouts. Sample error from our job: 

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/ingest.py\", line 210, in <module>
    embeddings = client.embeddings.create(model=\"embed-super-1\", input=batch)
  File \"/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/client.py\", line 84, in create
    raise EmbeddingError(\"Embedding dimension mismatch: expected %d got %d\" % (expected, got))
EmbeddingError: Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1538
```

beth_acme: Also seeing occasional HTTP 504 on some batches, others succeed. We roll retries ourselves (3 attempts) but some batches get duplications in reporting because we don't have idempotency tokens on per-item level.

alex_support: Thanks. Can you confirm full SDK versions (python/ts/go) used in the image and a sample payload shape (list lengths)? Also, do you send numpy arrays or lists?

beth_acme: Python worker uses redwood==1.2.2, ts service uses @redwood/sdk@0.9.8. Go is not used here. Input is a list[str] (UTF-8). Payload per batch: 128 strings, average length ~220 chars.

jamie_ml: Quick context from the model side: we rolled a quantized variant (embed-super-1-v2) to selected hosts last night that changes tokenization/padding behavior; vector size should be unchanged at 1536 though. That said, we did ship a small change in the upstream embedding postprocessing which can append 2 \"aux\" floats in some edge cases for streaming/KV metadata — shouldn't surface to API users but could if SDK mis-parses the payload.

alex_support: Sounds like a parsing bug in the SDK could be turning metadata into extra floats. Can SDK folks take a look?

Taylor_SDK_Py: I'll dig in. I can reproduce locally when batching: if you pass numpy arrays or certain float32 lists, our Python serializer adds a padding step that accidentally appends two zero floats when vector length inference is run on the response. Repro snippet: 

```python
# repro (python):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
texts = [\"short text\"] * 128
resp = client.embeddings.create(model=\"embed-super-1\", input=texts, batch_size=128, timeout=20)
# inspect first embedding length
print(len(resp.data[0].embedding))
```

Taylor_SDK_Py: In my runs len(...) toggles between 1536 and 1538 depending on when the response chunk boundary occurs. Looks like a bug in response deserialization where two padding floats from an internal stream frame are being interpreted as embedding floats for some frames. I'm opening a PR to strip trailing zeros if embedding length > expected and warn.

ravi_sdk_ts: On the TS side we saw a separate but related issue: the ts-sdk's default per-batch timeout is 10s and the retry logic immediately retries full batches on 504 without jitter or idempotency, so under load some requests get duplicated and push the server to slow paths causing dimension-edge frames to appear. We should add exponential jitter and per-item idempotency guidance. I'll prepare a patch to increase default batch timeout to 30s and add jittered backoff.

maria_eng: From infra, I confirmed the model variant switch was fragmentary during rollout for a subset of hosts in us-west-2 between 02:10-02:24 UTC. A small number of requests hit a host still returning legacy stream frames; combo of SDK deserializers and mixed-host rollout probably explains the intermittent nature. Server-side logs show those responses included an extra two floats flagged as \"stream_meta\" in internal frames. This is allowed internally but SDKs must filter them.

alex_support: Action items so far: 1) SDK teams to release patches that sanitize embeddings by truncating/padding to expected dim and log a metric when mismatch occurs, 2) TS SDK to harden retry/backoff defaults, 3) Ops to finish rollout and mark hosts stable, 4) ask customer to temporarily set batch_size=64 or increase per-request timeout.

Taylor_SDK_Py: Patch PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-python/pull/487 — implements safe-deserialize by checking model.metadata.vector_size (fallback 1536) and trimming trailing zeros if present. Will cut v1.2.3 patch after review. Also added a debug env REDWOOD_EMB_WARN_ON_TRIM=true for customers to opt-in warnings.

ravi_sdk_ts: PR for TS: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-js/pull/231 — increases timeout, adds 100-1000ms jitter and idempotency-key guidance in README. Will publish 0.9.9 shortly.

ci-bot: Deploy started for sdk-python v1.2.3 -> staging (job 5692).

maria_eng: Ops completed the model rollout at 02:45 UTC, verified consistent host responses. No more \"stream_meta\" frames leaking to public responses.

ci-bot: sdk-python v1.2.3 published (sha: a1b2c3d) and sdk-js v0.9.9 published (sha: d4e5f6).

beth_acme: Thanks team — upgraded python SDK to 1.2.3 and lowered batch_size to 64 as a precaution. After running ~24h they report no mismatches and much fewer 504s. Will keep at 64 for a week then try bumping. :thumbsup:

alex_support: Great. Can you confirm if any items were double-inserted into your DB due to retries? If so we can help with reconciliation scripts.

beth_acme: We found 14 duplicate batches in our ingest logs; we deduped by batch-id. No customer-facing duplicates.

alex_support: Perfect. Follow-ups: - Jamie / Maria, please add a unit test on server to assert stream_meta frames are never included in public embedding frames. - Taylor / Ravi, coordinate a minor release note about trimming behavior and retry defaults. - Beth, we'll keep monitoring.

jamie_ml: Adding server test to pipeline now.

maria_eng: Ticket created: INF-7829 \"prevent stream_meta leakage to public responses\".

alex_support: Closing this thread once Beth confirms stable for 72h. Thanks all.

beth_acme: Confirmed stable at +48h. We'll ping if anything else shows up. :rocket:
